PRENATAL CYTOGENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Regional Genetics Laboratory

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Hospital Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Amniotic Fluid
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Maternal Age: 35 years
Gestation: 16 weeks
Indication for Testing: Advanced maternal age - screening for common chromosomal trisomies

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)

METHODOLOGY
QF-PCR analysis was performed on uncultured amniocytes extracted from amniotic fluid. DNA was extracted using QIAamp DNA Mini Kit (Qiagen). Multiplex PCR amplification was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for short tandem repeat (STR) markers specific to chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. The following markers were analyzed:

Chromosome 13: D13S631, D13S258, D13S742, D13S628
Chromosome 18: D18S535, D18S391, D18S858, D18S386
Chromosome 21: D21S1435, D21S11, D21S1270, D21S1411

PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak areas were calculated using GeneMapper software v5.0.

RESULTS

Chromosome 13: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
- D13S631: 1.05 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D13S258: 1.12 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D13S742: Homozygous
- D13S628: 0.98 (normal range 0.8-1.4)

Chromosome 18: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
- D18S535: 1.08 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D18S391: 0.95 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D18S858: 1.14 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D18S386: Homozygous

Chromosome 21: Normal diallelic pattern observed for all informative markers
- D21S1435: 1.02 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D21S11: 0.91 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D21S1270: 1.09 (normal range 0.8-1.4)
- D21S1411: Homozygous

CONCLUSION
Results are consistent with a normal chromosome complement for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. No evidence of trisomy 13 (Patau syndrome), trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), or trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) detected in this fetal sample.

LIMITATIONS
1. This test assumes the presence of predominantly non-maternal fetal material in the sample. Maternal cell contamination cannot be completely excluded without additional testing.
2. QF-PCR cannot detect low-level mosaicism (<20%) for the chromosomes tested.
3. This test does not detect balanced chromosomal rearrangements or segmental imbalances.
4. This test only analyzes chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. Other chromosomal abnormalities will not be detected.
5. This test does not detect single gene disorders or microdeletion/microduplication syndromes.

RECOMMENDATIONS
No further chromosome analysis is required on this sample based on these results. Standard prenatal care and ultrasound monitoring should continue as per routine clinical practice.

Reported by: [redacted name], Clinical Scientist
Authorized by: [redacted name], Consultant Clinical Geneticist
Report Date: [redacted date]
